question: In a patient with a febrile urinary tract infection who is not improving on appropriate intravenous antibiotics, the surgeon must assume there is an obstructed system and arrange urgent decompression (nephrostomy or ureteric stent).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. A pyrexial UTI that does not respond to appropriate antibiotics should be assumed to have an obstruction until proven otherwise; emergency decompression is the surgical priority.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. An infected obstructed kidney will not clear with antibiotics alone; urgent drainage — percutaneous nephrostomy or retrograde ureteric stenting — is required to prevent irreversible renal damage and septic shock.
